title: Chapter 12 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of responsive design: viewport, media queries, fluid typography, responsive images, and navigation patterns!

questions.question: What does the viewport meta tag `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` do?
options: Makes the page adapt to the device's screen width
questions.explanation: It tells mobile browsers to match the viewport width to the device width and set initial zoom to 100%.

questions.question: Mobile‑first design means writing all styles for desktop first and then overriding them for mobile.
questions.explanation: Mobile‑first starts with the smallest screen styles (base) and uses `min-width` media queries to add complexity for larger screens.

questions.question: Which CSS unit is relative to the root element's font size?
questions.explanation: `rem` (root em) is relative to the font size of the `<html>` element.

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for a media query that applies only when the viewport is at least 768px wide?
questions.explanation: `min-width: 768px` triggers when the viewport width is 768px or more.

questions.question: Which value of `justify-content` distributes space evenly between grid/flex tracks including half‑space at the edges?
questions.explanation: `space-around` gives equal space around each item, resulting in half‑sized gaps at the ends.

questions.question: What does `clamp(1rem, 2vw + 0.5rem, 2rem)` do?
options: Allows the font size to scale between 1rem and 2rem based on viewport width
Creates a fixed font size of 1.5rem
questions.explanation: `clamp()` sets a minimum, a preferred value (which can be a calculation), and a maximum.

questions.question: In responsive images, the `sizes` attribute tells the browser how ______ the image will be displayed at different viewport widths.
questions.explanation: `sizes` describes the layout width of the image element so the browser can pick the best source.

questions.question: Which HTML element lets you provide different image sources based on media queries or format support?
questions.explanation: The `` element contains one or more `` elements and an `` fallback.

questions.question: The `srcset` attribute on an `` can specify multiple image files, and the browser picks the most appropriate one based on screen resolution and layout width.
questions.explanation: `srcset` with width descriptors (`w`) and `sizes` allow the browser to choose the optimal image.

questions.question: Which CSS Grid function creates as many columns as will fit in a container, each at least 200px and growing to fill space?
questions.explanation: `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr))` creates responsive columns without media queries.

questions.question: What does `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` target?
options: Users who have set their operating system to dark mode
questions.explanation: It applies styles when the user's OS is set to a dark colour scheme.

questions.question: In a mobile‑first approach, your base CSS should target:
options: The smallest screen size you support
questions.explanation: Base styles are for the smallest viewport; larger viewports override via `min-width` media queries.

questions.question: Why is it recommended to use `rem` for font sizes?
options: It respects the user's browser font size setting, improving accessibility
It makes the page load faster
questions.explanation: `rem` scales with the root font size, so users who increase default font size will see larger text.

questions.question: Which CSS property is used to create a smooth transition when an off‑canvas menu slides in?
questions.explanation: `transition` animates property changes, e.g., `transition: transform 0.3s;` for sliding menus.

questions.question: What does `aria-expanded="true"` on a hamburger button indicate?
questions.explanation: `aria-expanded="true"` tells assistive technology that the controlled element is expanded.

questions.question: Container queries allow styling an element based on the size of its parent container, not just the viewport.
questions.explanation: Container queries (using `container-type` and `@container`) are a recent CSS feature that enables component‑based responsive design.

questions.question: When using `<picture>` for art direction, what attribute on `<source>` determines which image is used?
questions.explanation: The `media` attribute accepts a media query; the first matching `<source>` is chosen.

questions.question: Which media query feature would you use to apply styles when a device is in landscape mode?
questions.explanation: `orientation: landscape` matches when the viewport is wider than it is tall.

questions.question: What is a common breakpoint for tablets in responsive design?
questions.explanation: 768px is a typical breakpoint where tablet layouts begin to differ from mobile.

questions.question: How can you make a flex layout stack items vertically on mobile and horizontally on desktop without media queries?
options: You can't; media queries are always needed
questions.explanation: `flex-direction: row` combined with `flex-wrap: wrap` and flexible widths (e.g., `flex: 1 1 300px`) can achieve stacking without media queries if items naturally wrap.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `initial-scale=1.0` in the viewport meta tag?
options: Sets the initial zoom level to 100%
questions.explanation: `initial-scale=1.0` ensures the page is not zoomed in or out when first loaded.

questions.question: Which HTML entity should you use to display a hamburger icon?
questions.explanation: `☰` is the trigram for heaven (☰), commonly used as a hamburger icon.

questions.question: On a responsive site, it's acceptable to serve the same 4MB desktop image to mobile users as long as the layout resizes.
questions.explanation: Performance matters; you should serve appropriately sized images to each device using responsive image techniques.

questions.question: Which CSS property can be used to hide an element visually but keep it accessible to screen readers?
options: A custom class like `.sr-only` with specific styles
questions.explanation: `display: none` and `visibility: hidden` remove from accessibility tree. A `.sr-only` class uses techniques like `position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden;` to hide visually but remain in the accessibility tree.

questions.question: In a responsive navigation, what is the primary purpose of the `aria-controls` attribute on a menu toggle button?
options: To associate the button with the element it controls (e.g., the menu)
questions.explanation: `aria-controls` links the button to the ID of the element it shows/hides, helping assistive technology understand the relationship.
